lenses.headline: The tree has exactly ONE cross-thread structured publisher (sound's PublishedChannel handshake) and it has zero production consumers — so HB-5 must ship as a naming rule plus a shape-constraint register, not as a `core::Published<T>`; the four references HB-5 currently cites are all wrong or Main-only.
lenses.rerun_trigger: Re-run this lens when ANY of the following becomes true, because each changes the one number the verdict rests on (count of real cross-thread structured publishers = 1): (a) a production thread spawn appears outside `xash3dpp/src/sound/topology.cpp` — grep `spawn_thread`/`std::thread` over `xash3dpp/src`; (b) the Chunk-12 thread-model decision is ratified in `decisions-architecture.md`; (c) `Sound::channels_snapshot()` acquires its first production (non-test) caller; (d) a new symbol matching `publish_*` or `*_snapshot` is added outside `src/server/clients/` — that is a 2nd/3rd bespoke mechanism appearing and it is exactly what the naming rule exists to catch; (e) Chunk 13 begins and `RenderFrame` acquires any code.

recommendations.title: Rewrite the HB-5 entry: the answer is a rule, not a primitive — and three of its four cited references are wrong
recommendations.what: Replace implementation-plan.md:591-599 with (a) the verdict 'no shared primitive is warranted today: one real cross-thread structured publisher exists and it has zero production consumers', (b) the Tier A–E classification table from this lens, (c) the shape-constraint set (core/ family membership, no >64-bit atomic, demand-driven pull, POD/string two-tier split, writers stay Main-pinned, alignof collision with HB-7, never the wire pipeline), and (d) corrections to the three false references: map_loader's WorldData swap is Main-only not cross-thread; server's snapshot_* is the wire entity-delta pipeline and server's only cross-thread surface is ServerStats; RenderFrame is zero code in xash3dpp/ and is gated on Chunk 13's unresolved GL-vs-Vulkan precondition. Name sound's topology.cpp:416-472 handshake and the LockedSfxResolver address-stability borrow as the two worked examples any future brief must start from.
recommendations.why: HB-5 is OPEN and reads as overdue buildable work. As written it would send an implementer to build a primitive for consumers that do not exist, guided by three citations that do not say what the entry claims. Two independent Phase-1 packs already mis-read server's snapshot_* as P-2 evidence because of this entry's wording. Correcting a backlog entry costs one document and prevents a whole implementation thread.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-5 (implementation-plan.md:591-599)
recommendations.named_consumer: The HB-5 brief itself plus every future reader of implementation-plan.md; builds no code.
recommendations.fence_note: Documentation only. No code touched, no HB-2 kernel implicated.

recommendations.title: Ratify a three-term publish/snapshot vocabulary rule as a register entry (Q-25 candidate)
recommendations.what: Add a decision-register entry reserving three terms tree-wide: `publish`/`published_*` only for a cross-thread one-writer/many-reader handoff where a second thread genuinely exists on that path; `snapshot` only for an owned caller-consumable copy of state at an instant (P-4 value types, thread-agnostic); `delta_frame`/`baseline` for the wire entity pipeline. Add the corollary that an accessor returning `const Stats &` into live Impl is never a snapshot, with MapLoader::stats() (map_loader.cpp:271, by value) named as the conforming precedent and Clock::stats()/Host::stats() named as the violations.
recommendations.why: 308 'snapshot' occurrences in xash3dpp/, 165 of them (54%) in server meaning network entity-delta. One word, three unrelated concepts, no way to tell from a symbol name which one you are reading. This is the root cause of the Phase-1 misreadings and it will recur in Chunk 12 when client work meets the delta pipeline. A naming rule builds nothing, so the anti-gold-plating rule does not bite, and it is worth more than the primitive it replaces.
recommendations.promotes_target: decisions-architecture.md §3 — new Q entry (next free number; Q-25 at time of writing)
recommendations.named_consumer: Chunks 11-14 authors and every future boundary spec; the rule constrains naming of code that already exists and code not yet written.
recommendations.fence_note: Convention only; no renames performed by this recommendation (see L1-R4 for the deferred rename).

recommendations.title: Record HB-5 as blocked-by the Chunk-12 thread-model decision instead of open-and-unstarted
recommendations.what: Mark HB-5's status as gated: its central question ('is a shared publish primitive warranted?') is decidable only once the Chunk-12 thread-model decision is ratified and Chunk 13's GL-vs-Vulkan precondition is resolved, because both determine whether a second long-lived thread ever exists outside src/sound/topology.cpp. Record the gate explicitly as a Chunk-12 precondition line so the decision surfaces where it will actually be made, and so HB-5 stops reading as overdue work in the backlog.
recommendations.why: Today the tree has exactly two production thread spawns, both in sound. Every argument for a shared primitive rests on there being more. Leaving HB-5 open-and-unstarted invites someone to discharge it speculatively; converting it to a gated item makes the real dependency visible at the point of decision. This is the honest form of 'brief-and-wait'.
recommendations.promotes_target: Chunk 12 (client) preconditions in implementation-plan.md; cross-linked from HB-5
recommendations.named_consumer: Chunk 12's thread-model decision, which is already a stated precondition of that chunk.
recommendations.blocked_by: Chunk-12 thread-model decision; Chunk-13 GL-vs-Vulkan decision

recommendations.title: Defer server's snapshot_*→delta_frame_* rename to Chunk 12 as a precondition, not as work now
recommendations.what: Record that server's ~165 `snapshot` tokens (src/server/clients/snapshot.cpp, private/server/snapshot.hpp, SnapshotState, snapshot_alloc_baselines/_ring/_signon, snapshot_reset, snapshot_shutdown) are wire entity-delta and violate the L1-R2 vocabulary rule, and schedule the rename as a Chunk-12 precondition to be executed when client work first touches the delta pipeline — not as a standalone sweep today.
recommendations.why: The rename is a pure ambiguity deletion with no behavioural content, but it is 165 sites in the file family that sits directly beside the HB-2-fenced networking bit-codec and delta field widths. Doing it standalone is churn with parity-review cost and no consumer; doing it when Chunk 12 is already opening those files is nearly free. Recording it now stops the next auditor from re-finding it as a fresh problem.

But the delta FIELD WIDTHS and bit-codec in networking are fenced: rename identifiers only, never touch field ordering, widths, or codec arithmetic.

recommendations.title: Record Cvar::generation as a publisher with zero consumers in the cmd_cvar boundary spec's P-2 row
recommendations.what: Add a boundary-spec row stating that `Cvar::generation` (cvar.hpp:130) has two release publishers (cvar_ops.cpp:204 and :370, both `fetch_add(1, memory_order_release)`) and ZERO consumers — no `.load()` on it exists anywhere in src/, include/ or tests/. Record the decision to KEEP it (4 bytes per Cvar plus one release fetch_add per write; it is the tree's only ready-made lock-free change-epoch and the natural first test case for any HB-5 brief) together with the explicit caveat that it is NOT evidence of a working publish mechanism and must not be cited as one or imitated by copy.
recommendations.why: The lens brief itself carried the claim 'cmd_cvar's generation counter with no publisher at all', which is exactly backwards — a fact-base error this lens can only correct by having read the code. Without a boundary row saying 'publisher exists, consumer does not, deliberately', the next audit will either re-find it as a defect or count it toward HB-5's mechanism tally. Both have already happened to other surfaces in this campaign.

recommendations.title: Name HB-5 as a requirer on the HB-7 aligned-allocation entry
recommendations.what: Add one line to HB-7 (shared aligned-allocation door) recording HB-5 as a named future requirer: any double-buffer or seqlock publish primitive that wants `alignas(64)` false-sharing separation between its two slots cannot be `pool_new`'d, because memory.hpp:127 hard-asserts `alignof(T) <= 8` (Q-22). Today HB-7's only cited driver is G-5's allocator hooks, which has no chunk number — this gives it a second, more concrete requirer.
recommendations.why: HB-7 was refuted as work in this campaign precisely because its only consumer was self-declared speculative. This is a cross-backlog dependency that no per-subsystem pack could see: it only appears when you compare memory's pool_new constraint against what a publish primitive would need. Recording it costs one line and materially strengthens HB-7's case when its time comes.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-7 (implementation-plan.md aligned-allocation door entry)

recommendations.fence_note: Documentation only. Explicitly does NOT propose lifting alignof(T) <= 8 — that was already refuted this campaign.

shape_constraints.constraint: Any published-snapshot primitive lives in xash3dpp/include/xash3dpp/core/ as the third member of the mpsc_queue.hpp / spsc_ring.hpp family and matches their house style exactly: template on the payload, `static_assert(std::is_trivially_copyable_v<T>)`, fixed compile-time capacity, zero allocation after construction, explicit 64-bit cursors, `static_assert(std::atomic<pos_t>::is_always_lock_free)`.
shape_constraints.applies_when: HB-5's primitive is ever built (earliest: Chunk 13 RenderFrame).

shape_constraints.constraint: The primitive must not require an atomic wider than 64 bits. x86 ships and there is no portable DWCAS, which rules out a tagged {pointer, sequence} swap and points at seqlock-over-POD or double-buffer-with-atomic-index.
shape_constraints.applies_when: HB-5's primitive is ever built.

shape_constraints.constraint: Publication must be demand-driven (request/ack pull), not per-frame push. The one working in-tree mechanism (topology.cpp:416-472) publishes only when Main raises snapshot_request_, spins a bounded number of yields, and falls back to the last published value on exhaustion. A publish-every-frame double-buffer puts cold introspection cost on the hot path.
shape_constraints.applies_when: HB-5's primitive is ever built.

shape_constraints.constraint: Two explicit tiers, not one. POD payloads ride the lock-free primitive; string-bearing payloads (PublishedChannel::sentence_name, ModelInfo::name, BindingEntry, GameInfo's ten std::strings, MusicState's two) are copied out under a lock. This is already what sound (publish_mutex_) and filesystem (shared_mutex) do. A single tier attempting to cover both will fail.
shape_constraints.applies_when: HB-5's primitive is ever built, or any new snapshot type is added.

shape_constraints.constraint: P-2 relaxes the READ side only. Writer and lifecycle Main-pinning survives a published-snapshot design — single-publisher discipline is the mechanism. Content's 12 assert_thread_role(Main) sites (model_cache.cpp:81,95,123,158,191,212,224,239,312 + imagelib.cpp:54,61,73) are all writers/lifecycle and are PERMANENT under P-2. What is missing is a read-side assert on resolve()/find()/model_infos().
shape_constraints.applies_when: Any subsystem adopts a published-snapshot read path.

shape_constraints.constraint: An accessor returning `const Stats &` into live Impl state is never a snapshot, whatever it is named. The conforming precedent is MapLoader::stats() returning by value (map_loader.cpp:271). Clock::stats() (clock.cpp:258, zero callers) and Host::stats() (host.cpp:345) are the violations.
shape_constraints.applies_when: Any stats or introspection accessor is added or reviewed.
shape_constraints.record_in: core-boundary.md + host-boundary.md P-2 rows; enforced by the L1-R2 register entry

shape_constraints.constraint: The HB-5 primitive is never the vehicle for the wire entity-delta pipeline. server's SnapshotState/packet_entities/baselines ring is Main-only, netchan-consumed, and sits beside the HB-2-fenced bit-codec and delta field widths.
shape_constraints.applies_when: Any refactor touches src/server/clients/snapshot.cpp.

shape_constraints.constraint: A double-buffer wanting alignas(64) false-sharing separation cannot be pool_new'd — memory.hpp:127 asserts alignof(T) <= 8. Either the primitive stays 8-byte-alignable or HB-7 must land first.
shape_constraints.applies_when: HB-5's primitive is built with cacheline padding.

shape_constraints.constraint: When the primitive is specified, the LockedSfxResolver pattern (mutex-on-lookup + a hard address-stability invariant: reserve-to-max at construction, refuse to grow, never free) must be evaluated as an ALTERNATIVE to snapshotting, not merely as prior art. It is the tree's only mechanism that gets structured Main-owned data to a worker thread with zero copying, and it works in production today.
shape_constraints.applies_when: The HB-5 brief is written.

lenses.headline: Four extension-keyed dispatch sites, three incompatible shapes, and three different answers to the same legacy `Q_stricmp` contract — one of them a live parity divergence; making the extension key mandatory collapses all three shapes, deletes two `handles()` virtual hierarchies and one drift-prone parallel table, and is a net deletion.
lenses.rerun_trigger: Re-run L2 when ANY of the following becomes true: (1) a 5th extension- or magic-keyed dispatch site appears — the Chunk 13 renderer backend selector is the expected trigger, followed by a demo format/version selector or a G-5 script-format loader; (2) any new per-implementation key predicate (`handles()`, `accepts()`, `supported()`, `can_load()`) is added to an `I*` interface, since that is the exact anti-pattern the canonical shape bans and it has already been independently invented twice; (3) a second parallel key-only array shadowing a dispatch table is introduced; (4) a new enumerator is added to `DeltaTableSet`, `AllocStrategy`, or any other closed-set dispatch key while L2-R5's `/w14062` gate is still unlanded; (5) HB-13 lands only partially — i.e. the convention subsection is written but any of the three conversions (R2/R3/R4) is still open at the start of Chunk 13, because the renderer will then be authored against a rule with no working exemplar.

recommendations.title: Codify ONE extension-keyed dispatch-table idiom in the binding conventions, and open HB-13 to carry the three conversions
recommendations.what: Add a subsection under `.github/instructions/xash3dpp.instructions.md` §"Registries and Handles" (:148-164) covering the compile-time dispatch table the existing four rules do not mention: (a) a mandatory `std::string_view key` first column, read at dispatch — a per-implementation `handles()`/`accepts()` predicate is banned as a dispatch key; (b) exactly one comparison, `utilities::ci_equal`, matching legacy `Q_stricmp`, so callers never pre-lowercase; (c) declaration order is load-bearing where the domain has priority and must say so; (d) any "is X supported?" query is answered from the SAME table via a nullable payload or a flag column — a parallel key-only array is banned. Open HB-13 in `implementation-plan.md` (HOUSE, no design brief — it is a convention plus three mechanical conversions) carrying R2/R3/R4 as items and the acceptance criterion 'a new format author touches 3 files, 0 of which can fail silently'.
recommendations.why: Three shapes exist because the written convention is silent on the key and the lookup — all three are conformant with the four rules as written, which is why no reviewer caught it. Legacy solved this once (`filesystem.c:91`, `img_main.c:278`, `snd_utils.c:454`); the rewrite produced three answers and one parity bug. Codifying is the only way the Chunk 13 renderer backend selector does not become the fourth shape.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-13 — One extension-keyed dispatch-table idiom (conventions subsection + 3 conversions)
recommendations.named_consumer: k_archive_types / k_wad_types / k_audio_codecs / imagelib registry[] — 4 existing dispatch sites
recommendations.fence_note: Clear. No HB-2 kernel and no frozen-ABI file is touched: all four tables are xash3dpp-internal, and the legacy `Q_stricmp` behaviour being matched is the parity target, not a deviation from it.

recommendations.title: Merge `k_audio_codecs` and `k_audio_extensions` into one nullable-accessor table and delete `IAudioCodec::handles`
recommendations.what: Make `k_audio_codecs` the single 4-row table `{{"wav",&wav_codec},{"mp3",nullptr},{"ogg",nullptr},{"opus",nullptr}}`; `find_audio_codec` becomes `if (ci_equal(e.key, ext) && e.codec) return &e.codec();`; `is_supported_audio_extension` becomes the same scan without the null check. DELETE `k_audio_extensions` (codec.hpp:106), DELETE the pure virtual `IAudioCodec::handles` (codec.hpp:49) and `WavCodec`'s override (codec_wav.cpp:408) with its duplicated "wav" literal, DELETE the `to_lower` heap allocation at registry.cpp:58 (ci_equal removes the need). Update the 7 asserts in tests/sound/test_sound_codec.cpp:137-161 that pin the two-table shape.
recommendations.why: The declared key column is dead in production — `find_audio_codec` (codec.hpp:124-133) ignores `entry.extension` entirely and instantiates every codec singleton to ask `handles(ext)`, which then re-hardcodes the identical literal. The two tables can disagree in the undesigned direction (codec row present, extension row absent) with no compile-time, runtime, or test diagnostic. This is the single change that removes the drift risk and the dead column together, and it is a pure deletion: −1 table, −1 pure virtual, −1 override, −1 literal, −1 allocation.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-13 item B
recommendations.named_consumer: FilesystemAudioLoader::load (src/sound/registry.cpp:61,71) — the only production caller of find_audio_codec
recommendations.fence_note: Clear. Sound's HB-2 exposure is the mix kernel and the DSP float chain, neither of which is on the codec-selection path. The S9.8 determinism witness compares PCM for a fixed console script and is unaffected by which table row selected the wav codec. Blast radius 15: 6 production sites + 2 call sites + 7 test asserts (grep `handles(|find_audio_codec` over src/sound, private/sound, tests/sound).

recommendations.title: Give imagelib's keyless pointer array a key column and delete `IImageCodec::handles` and its 7 overrides
recommendations.what: Add `struct ImageCodecEntry { std::string_view key; const IImageCodec &(*codec)() noexcept; }` plus `inline constexpr std::array<ImageCodecEntry,7> k_image_codecs` to `include/xash3dpp/private/imagelib/codec.hpp` DIRECTLY BELOW the seven accessor declarations at :36-44, so declaration and registration are one screen apart instead of two files apart. Replace the function-local `static const IImageCodec *const registry[]` at imagelib.cpp:94-102 with a `ci_equal` scan of that table. DELETE the pure virtual `handles` (codec.hpp:26) and all seven one-line overrides (codec_bmp.cpp:306, codec_dds.cpp:394, codec_ktx2.cpp:240, codec_mip.cpp:288, codec_png.cpp:418, codec_tga.cpp:228, codec_wad.cpp:141). DELETE the local `extension_of` and the 16-char lowercase buffer (imagelib.cpp:25-31, :80-90) in favour of `utilities::file_extension` + `ci_equal` — imagelib already links xash3dpp_utilities PUBLIC (content/CMakeLists.txt:34).
recommendations.why: This is the only dispatch site in the tree with no key at all, so nothing outside can ask 'is .png an image format?' without instantiating seven singletons and running a decode probe — and Chunk 13 is the caller that will ask. A codec declared in codec.hpp but omitted from the function-local array compiles, links and silently never dispatches. The hand-rolled lowercase also carries a real defect: `n = ext.size() < lo.size() ? ext.size() : 0` yields the EMPTY extension (not a truncated one) for any extension ≥16 chars, so such a file gets `UnknownFormat` rather than a miss.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-13 item C
recommendations.named_consumer: ImageDecoder::decode (src/content/imagelib/imagelib.cpp:104) — the function being restructured; Chunk 13 renderer is the downstream asker
recommendations.fence_note: Clear. content's HB-2 kernel is studio bone math; imagelib is a separate CMake target that does not touch it. Blast radius 9 production sites (7 overrides + 1 pure virtual + 1 loop), 0 external callers of `handles()` (grep over src/content, private/imagelib, tests/content). Best landed BEFORE Chunk 13 links xash3dpp_imagelib — the blast radius only grows once the renderer is a second caller.

recommendations.title: Fix the case-sensitive archive-extension compare — a live parity divergence, two lines
recommendations.what: Replace `ext.substr(1) != at.extension` (src/filesystem/filesystem.cpp:68) and `ext != at.extension` (:336) with `!xash::utilities::ci_equal(...)`. Add a regression test mounting a mixed-case archive name.
recommendations.why: Legacy `filesystem.c:3441` and `FS_AddGameDirectory` compare with `Q_stricmp`; xash3dpp compares with `!=`. A game directory containing `FOO.PAK` (or any archive with a non-lowercase extension — routine on case-preserving Windows filesystems and in redistributed mod content) mounts under legacy and is silently skipped by xash3dpp, with no log line on the collect path. The sibling table in the SAME subsystem (`k_wad_types`, wad_backend.cpp:90) already uses `ci_equal` correctly — this is intra-subsystem inconsistency, not a design tradeoff.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-13 item A
recommendations.named_consumer: Filesystem::mount_archive and collect_paths_for_dir — both production, both on the startup path
recommendations.fence_note: Clear. filesystem is not one of the five HB-2 kernel subsystems and archive-extension matching is not byte-exact-constrained; the change moves TOWARD legacy behaviour, so any parity witness that changes was asserting the divergence.

recommendations.title: Make closed-set exhaustiveness an actual build gate (`/w14062`), and convert `delta_wire_format_for`'s ternary to a defaultless switch
recommendations.what: Add `/w14062` to the MSVC branch of `xash3dpp/CMakeLists.txt:16` (GCC/Clang already emit `-Wswitch` by default for enums without a default label). Then convert `delta_wire_format_for` (private/networking/delta/wire_format.hpp:58) from a 2-way ternary to a `switch` over `DeltaTableSet` with no `default:`, and DELETE its comment obligation 'Extend this switch when a new DeltaTableSet value is introduced' — the compiler now owns it.
recommendations.why: Two sites document a safety property the build does not enforce: palette.cpp:161 claims 'no default (compiler-checked exhaustiveness)' and wire_format.hpp:57 writes the obligation as prose over a construct (a ternary) that cannot be checked at all — a new DeltaTableSet enumerator silently maps to the Xash format. The build sets only `/EHs-c- /GR- /fp:precise`; C4062 is level 4 and silent at CMake's default `/W3`. This is the cheapest available conversion of a prose obligation into a gate, and it protects every future closed-set dispatch including the Chunk 13 backend selector. Bounded risk: 57 switch sites in src/ carry 52 `default:` labels, so at most ~5 sites can fire, and int-keyed switches (movetype, contents, fieldType) are not enums and cannot.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-13 item D (or a sibling HOUSE entry if the build-flag change is routed separately)
recommendations.named_consumer: Every enum-keyed switch in the tree; the immediate beneficiary is DeltaTableSet (wire_format.hpp:58) and AudioCommandType (audio_command.cpp:288)
recommendations.fence_note: Clear, with one caution: `/w14062` is a diagnostic-only flag and cannot alter codegen, so no HB-2 kernel output can shift. The `delta_wire_format_for` edit selects between the same two existing singletons and emits no bytes itself — but it sits adjacent to the networking wire bit-codec fence, so the change must be a pure control-flow rewrite with no reordering of the format objects' own logic.

recommendations.title: Record the dispatch leave-verdicts and the client-command growth trigger as boundary-spec rows, so nobody re-litigates or silently outgrows them

lenses.headline: The tree has 14 stats structs and four mutually-contradictory `stats()` contracts; the real G-3 blocker is not "9 plain structs" but 6 accessors that hand back a live reference into plain memory — and 3 of those 6 are deletable outright. The §6.2 positional `diagnostics_dump` sketch is not merely unscalable, it is unbuildable: host does not link sound/input/content/imagelib, so the positional form demands 4 new link edges while a channel-span form demands zero.
lenses.rerun_trigger: Re-run L3 when ANY of these fires — each invalidates a specific conclusion above, and none is a date: (1) **a 15th stats struct is added**, or any existing one changes its accessor return kind — the four-class table and the "6 in class D" count are the whole basis of the retrofit costing; (2) **`xash3dpp_host` gains a link edge to sound, input, content or imagelib** — that single fact is what makes the positional §6.2 form unbuildable and the channel-span form free, so if it changes, re-argue L3-R1's shape from scratch; (3) **the first off-Main reader of any `stats()` or `*_snapshot()` surface is written** — i.e. the first G-1 or G-3 code, or a third production thread spawn beyond the two in `src/sound/topology.cpp` — which converts most of the shape constraints here into work with a real consumer; (4) **a fifth enumerated-row introspection channel appears**, or a second `log_set_callback` registrant lands — both mean the channel taxonomy in §3 has stopped describing the tree; (5) **HB-5 ratifies a published-snapshot idiom** — the correlated-tuple half of SC-1 defers to it and must be rewritten against whatever it actually says; (6) **a boundary spec is written for physics, client, renderer, demo, ui or world** — six 0-TU skeletons currently contribute silence, not health, to this inventory, and each new spec adds a stats row that this lens has not seen.

recommendations.title: Build the diagnostics aggregator as a channel span, not a positional parameter list, and land the `stats` console command that consumes it
recommendations.what: Add to core: `struct DiagSink { void (*write)(std::string_view, void*) noexcept; void *ud; };`, `struct DiagChannel { const char *name; void (*emit)(const void *self, const DiagSink &) noexcept; const void *self; };` and `void diagnostics_dump(std::span<const DiagChannel>, const DiagSink &) noexcept;`. Host assembles a fixed `std::array<DiagChannel, N>` from the subsystems it already owns and registers a `stats` built-in via `cmd_add`, with the sink writing to the console. Each participating subsystem exposes one captureless `emit` adapter that formats its own `stats()` into sink lines. Explicitly rejects `debug-stats-design.md:359`'s positional form.
recommendations.why: The positional form is not merely unscalable at 14 subsystems (P-5) — it is unbuildable without inverting the layer model: `xash3dpp_host` links cmd_cvar/core/filesystem/map_loader/memory/networking/platform/server and does NOT link sound/input/content/imagelib, so `diagnostics_dump(CmdCvarContext&, MemorySubsystem&, ...)` forces four new link edges into the composition root for a debug command. The span form forces zero: the root registers only what it owns, and the signature never changes as more subsystems are wired. The fn-ptr+void* channel row is the tree's existing callback convention (40+ `cmd_add` sites, `for_each_pool`), not a new abstraction — no std::function, no RTTI, no exceptions, alignof<=8, identical on x86/x64. This is the deliverable that discharges the `debug-stats-design.md` §6.4 trigger, overdue since the tree had 3 stats structs.
recommendations.promotes_target: HB-6 — Name the "one introspection layer" (P-4) channels (implementation-plan.md:601-609); this recommendation is the design-brief content HB-6 asks for, plus its first buildable slice

recommendations.title: Fix the stats() accessor contract to one rule and apply it to the four surviving class-D structs
recommendations.what: Record in debug-stats-design.md §6.1 and in each subsystem's boundary-spec stats row: **atomic storage may return `const&`; plain storage MUST return by value.** Then flip the four surviving offenders to by-value: `Content::stats()` (content.hpp:89), `Imagelib::stats()` (imagelib.hpp:55), `Filesystem::stats()` (filesystem.hpp:162), `StringPool::stats()` (private/server/string_pool.hpp:84). One-line change each; `MapLoader::stats()` (map_loader.cpp:271) and `memory::get_stats` are the in-tree precedents.
recommendations.why: Four accessor contracts exist today for one concept, and nothing has ever read them — which is exactly how a fifth arrives by Chunk 14. By-value does not make cross-thread reads torn-free (be honest about that: it removes the lifetime hazard, not the race), but it removes the worst property — handing a caller an alias into memory the owner will rewrite — and it is the shape the aggregator in L3-R1 needs to copy safely. The rule must be written down, not just applied, because save-boundary.md already promises a SaveStats that does not exist (F131/F134) and will otherwise be built to the wrong shape.

lenses.headline: The engine internals ARE context-carrying and the context-free reach is confined to two files — G-2's P-3 door is genuinely open. recommendations.what: `EngineBridge::sv_time` (engine_bridge.hpp:96) is read at engine_table.cpp:100, 711, 1097 and 2245 and assigned nowhere in `xash3dpp/src` (only tests/server/abi/test_engine_table.cpp:145). It drives EdictArena's legacy slot-reuse policy, which internal callers drive with the real `rt.level.time`. Fix: assign `rt.bridge.sv_time = rt.level.time` wherever the server frame advances level time (the same place `merge_visibility` is already maintained, snapshot.cpp:228/231/887), and add a regression test that frees an edict via pfnRemoveEntity at t>2.0 and asserts the 0.5s grace is honoured. Same pass: wire `novis` from the `sv_novis` cvar and `autoaim_threshold` from `sv_aim`/`sv_allow_autoaim` (both read, never written), and DELETE `group_mask`/`group_op` from EngineBridge (written at :2033-2034, read nowhere; the live copies are `move_env->group_mask` and `links->set_group_op`).

With sv_time frozen at 0.0, edicts freed through the game ABI satisfy `freetime < 2.0f` forever, so they are recycled by the next pfnCreateEntity with no grace window (EHANDLE / entity-index aliasing in the delta pipeline); symmetrically, `(0.0 - freetime) > 0.5` is never true, so the ABI create path never reuses internally-freed slots and grows the arena toward the 'no free edicts' error. Neither stub_scan, compliance_scan, nor the build can see 'declared, read, never written' — HB-11's inventory mechanism explicitly depends on inline stub markers, and there are none. Four fields survived Chunk 6B, a consolidation audit, a close-out audit and 35 packs.
